payload.prompt:
Create a Europa Universalis V Engineering Department module cover PNG asset.
Subject: Create a square Steam Workshop cover illustration for the standalone Engineering Department sub-mod of Towards Victory, in the epic historical key-art style of a AAA grand strategy game box cover, not a flat clean icon. Show a monumental wonder rising from a grand construction site at golden-hour dusk: scaffolding, a crane or hoist, pale marble blocks, and restrained bronze and gold accents, wrapped in atmospheric haze, dust, and dramatic warm light so it feels like a real moment of history being built. Use the two uploaded references only for guidance: take the construction-site motifs from the building icon reference, and take the painterly atmosphere, dramatic lighting, and epic mood from the tree-background reference. Compose off-center on a rule-of-thirds grid, with the wonder and its scaffolding positioned toward the lower third or one side of the frame. Leave the center of the composition calm, uncluttered, and free of important detail (open sky, drifting haze, or a soft receding backdrop) because a game title will later be overlaid there.
Reference image: use the uploaded target-specific reference image only as style guidance for palette, brushwork, lighting, surface treatment, and framing discipline. Do not copy its subject, exact composition, silhouette, ornament placement, or any text.
Distinctiveness: keep the result in the same visual family as the reference, but make it visibly different at a glance through changed shape language, object arrangement, cropping, or decorative accents.
Composition: keep the main subject centered, readable, and high-contrast, with no watermark, no letters, no logo, and no UI chrome baked into the art.
Target format: final PNG target is exactly 512x512 and must stay under 1,000,000 bytes.
Target-specific requirement: This is a square Steam Workshop/launcher cover image for the standalone Engineering Department sub-mod, not a small in-game icon. Aim for the epic, historical box-art quality of a AAA grand strategy game cover (Paradox-style key art): dramatic cinematic lighting such as a golden-hour sky or torch-lit dusk, atmospheric haze/dust, rich painterly detail, and a genuine sense of monumental scale and history in the making, not a flat clean icon render. Compose off-center using a rule-of-thirds layout: place the monumental wonder and its construction scene toward one side or the lower third of the frame, and keep the center of the image visually calm and uncluttered (sky, haze, or receding background) because a game title will be overlaid there later — do not put the main subject, the crane, or any important detail in the dead center. No text, no letters, no logo, no UI frame, no watermark.
Style rules:
Match the palette, brush feel, lighting, icon density, and framing discipline of the selected target's reference image. Keep the final subject and asset meaning driven by the selected batch entry, not the reference subject.
Extra composition rules:
Use the reference only as a style guide. Keep the result in the same visual family, but make it visibly distinct at a glance by changing the silhouette, crop, object arrangement, and ornament placement. Do not mirror the reference composition or reuse its exact outline.
Avoid:
text, letters, numbers, logo, watermark, UI frame, flat clean vector icon, simple centered icon composition, subject or main detail placed in the exact center, symmetrical center-locked framing, realistic photo, crowd of tiny unreadable details, finished/completed monument with no construction elements, blank empty background, flat lighting, low contrast
